default_reproduction: Exact guaranteed scores, root matrix, executions, nodes and stop reason match the archived g23 fixed-strategy control.
strategy_tests: Both sides; awake/frozen active; frozen/fainted bench; first-action override; complete one-turn expectations; switched-in continuation; Freeze Clause protection; group selection without state merging; exhaustive two-turn value enclosure.
conclusions: The complete four-cell first-transition census uses 528 engine executions. Ice Beam versus Earthquake has mass 0.845947265625 immediate side-one win, 0.0625 critical Marowak KO with forced replacement, 0.0826120376586914 frozen surviving Marowak, and 0.008940696716308594 thawed surviving Marowak.

A frozen bench prevents opponent-induced freeze on the switch-in. The fixed strategy switches a frozen active to the first legal nonfrozen bench. Removing voluntary switches from its normal priority prevents switching back from Suicune to frozen Marowak and allows Surf as the legal fallback.

At the standard caps, the corrected frozen-switch strategy plus chance-status grouping guarantees at least 0.9769382036439039, versus control 0.8977268717079653. It uses all 2,000,000 executions and 119,345 nodes; the control stops at its node cap after 742,188 executions. This is not a matched-execution strength comparison.

Doubling both caps gives a guarantee of 0.9796681926217522, stopping at 240,000 nodes after 2,992,094 executions. Both archived first-decision loss upper bounds shrink from 0.1022731285 to 0.0203318076, with 1e-10 outward padding. They remain above the 0.02 threshold.

Grouping alone and the corrected strategy alone did not improve the control certificate at standard caps. Overlapping restricted-strategy intervals do not rank actual policy strength. Both optional features remain disabled by default.

The largest remaining single root uncertainty is the critical-KO forced replacement branch: mass 0.0625 times continuation width 0.1509350111 contributes 0.0094334382 to the parent interval. This identifies a concrete 1v1 subproblem for further analysis.

No deployed bot changes or positive archived first-decision loss lower bounds are established. These are full-information first-decision certificates with optimal continuation, not global optimality or deployed blind-policy exploitability.
